chunks: Part of it, in the era of the Umayyad dynasty:

At that time, no house of stone or tent of hair will remain but that the oppressors will enter it with grief, and they will inject it with vengeance. On that day, no excuse will remain for them in the sky, nor any helper on the earth.
You selected for the authority one who was not its fit person, and you raised him to a position not meant for him,
and Allah will take revenge from whoever oppressed, food for food and drink for drink,
namely (they will be given) colocynth for eating, myrrh and aloes for drinking, and fear for an inner garment, and the sword for an outer covering.

key_terms.مَأْكَلاً بِمَأْكَلٍ: Food for food (retribution matching the deed)
key_terms.مَطَاعِمِ الْعَلْقَمِ: Foods of the colocynth (a bitter plant)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'food for food' in the Umayyad era sermon?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha’s sermon on the Umayyad era depicts the total penetration of injustice into both rural and urban dwellings, emphasizing that the caliphate was entrusted to the unworthy will face divine retribution. The imagery of 'food for food' and 'drink for drink' alludes to the specific bitter substances consumed by the oppressors as a precise measure of their guilt, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of cosmic justice. It underscores the transition from earthly political failure to inevitable heavenly accountability, where no earthly defender can intervene.
